conventions: STATED: the fact is directly asserted in the prose, including standard bio parenthetical conventions ((birthdate, birthplace - deathdate, deathplace)) and direct spousal terms (widow of, queen consort of).

ENTAILED: not directly asserted but a competent reader must conclude it: inverse kinship plus a gender cue (son of actress X -> mother; daughter of X and his wife Y -> mother), office implying the relation (UN High Commissioner -> works at UN; Sultan of the Ottoman Empire -> Ottoman nationality), alma-mater phrasing, Arabic patronymic (bin Nawwaf = son of Nawwaf).

ABSENT: not stated and not entailed; includes relation-ambiguous truncations (a bare place in a cut-off parenthetical), lookalike mentions (Saqqara only inside 'South Saqqara Stone'), adjacent-but-different relations (lives in / buried in / departed from vs born in / died in), and prose that contradicts the gold (Cazals 'registered as born in Mexico' vs gold France).
